e-6179.knowledge_point: Calculating the Equation of a Tangent Plane
e-6179.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z= x^2 + xy$ at the point $(1,2, 3).$
e-6179.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $(x_0, y_0, z_0)$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z - z_0 = (x-x_0)\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x}(x_0,y_0) + (y-y_0)\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y}(x_0,y_0).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+xy) \\  & =2x+y \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+xy) \\  & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y) = (1,2)\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,2) & =2(1)+2=4 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,2) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-3 & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,2)+(y-2)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,2) \\ z-3 & =4(x-1)+1(y-2) \\ z-3 & =4x+y-6 \\ -4x-y+z+3 & =0 \\ 4x+y-z-3 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

e-6185.knowledge_point: Calculating the Equation of a Tangent Hyperplane
e-6185.problem: Find the equation of the tangent hyperplane to the hypersurface $w=x^2+y^2+z^2-2xyz$ at the point $(1,-1,1,5).$
e-6185.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $w=f(x,y,z)$ at the point $(x_0, y_0, z_0,w_0)$ on the hypersurface can be written as

$$
w - w_0 = (x-x_0)\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x}(x_0,y_0,z_0) + (y-y_0)\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y}(x_0,y_0,z_0) + (z-z_0)\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial z}(x_0,y_0,z_0).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}-2xyz)=2x-2yz \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}-2xyz)=2y-2xz \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}-2xyz)=2z-2xy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y,z) = (1,-1,1)\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,-1,1) & =2(1)-2(-1)(1)=4 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,-1,1) & =2(-1)-2(1)(1)=-4 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z}(1,-1,1) & =2(1)-2(1)(-1)=4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent hyperplane:

$$
\begin{aligned}w-5 & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,-1,1)+(y+1)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,-1,1)+(z-1)\frac{∂f}{∂z}(1,-1,1)\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting and simplifying, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}w-5 & =4(x-1)-4(y+1)+4(z-1) \\ w-5 & =4x-4y+4z-12 \\ -4x+4y-4z+w+7 & =0 \\ 4x-4y+4z-w-7 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y-{y}^{3}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2xy \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y-{y}^{3}) \\  & =2xy+{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(1,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,2) & =3(1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+2(1)(2)=11 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,2) & =2(1)(2)+{1}^{2}-3(2)^{2}=-7\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-(-1) & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,2)+(y-2)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,2) \\ z+1 & =11(x-1)-7(y-2) \\ z+1 & =11x-7y+3 \\ -11x+7y+z-2 & =0 \\ 11x-7y-z+2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z={x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y-{y}^{3}$ at the point $(1,2,-1).$
content.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y-{y}^{3}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2xy \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y-{y}^{3}) \\  & =2xy+{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(1,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,2) & =3(1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+2(1)(2)=11 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,2) & =2(1)(2)+{1}^{2}-3(2)^{2}=-7\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-(-1) & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,2)+(y-2)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,2) \\ z+1 & =11(x-1)-7(y-2) \\ z+1 & =11x-7y+3 \\ -11x+7y+z-2 & =0 \\ 11x-7y-z+2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=x\sqrt{y}-y\sqrt{x}$ at the point $(1,4,-2).$
after.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\sqrt{y}-y\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\sqrt{y}-\frac{y}{2\sqrt{x}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\sqrt{y}-y\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\frac{x}{2\sqrt{y}}-\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(1,4):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,4) & =\sqrt{4}-\frac{4}{2\sqrt{1}}=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,4) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{4}}-\sqrt{1}=-\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-(-2) & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,4)+(y-4)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,4) \\ z+2 & =0(x-1)-\frac{3}{4}(y-4) \\ z+2 & =-\frac{3}{4}y+3 \\ \frac{3}{4}y+z-1 & =0 \\ 3y+4z-4 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=x\sqrt{y}-y\sqrt{x}$ at the point $(1,4,-2).$
content.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\sqrt{y}-y\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\sqrt{y}-\frac{y}{2\sqrt{x}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\sqrt{y}-y\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\frac{x}{2\sqrt{y}}-\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(1,4):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,4) & =\sqrt{4}-\frac{4}{2\sqrt{1}}=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,4) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{4}}-\sqrt{1}=-\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-(-2) & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,4)+(y-4)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,4) \\ z+2 & =0(x-1)-\frac{3}{4}(y-4) \\ z+2 & =-\frac{3}{4}y+3 \\ \frac{3}{4}y+z-1 & =0 \\ 3y+4z-4 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}-7) \\  & =8x \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}-7) \\  & =18y\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(1,-1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,-1) & =8(1)=8 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,-1) & =18(-1)=-18\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-6 & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,-1)+(y-(-1))\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,-1) \\ z-6 & =8(x-1)-18(y+1) \\ z-6 & =8x-18y-26 \\ 8x-18y-z-20 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Find the equation of the tangent hyperplane to the hypersurface $w=z\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1)$ at the point $(0,0,3,0).$
after.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the hypersurface $w=f(x,y,z)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0},{w}_{0})$ on the hypersurface can be written as

$$
w-{w}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(z-{z}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂z}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1))=\frac{2xz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(z\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1))=\frac{2yz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(z\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1))=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y,z)=(0,0,3):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(0,0,3) & =\frac{2(0)(3)}{{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}+1}=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(0,0,3) & =\frac{2(0)(3)}{{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}+1}=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z}(0,0,3) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({0}^{2}+{0}^{2}+1)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent hyperplane:

$$
\begin{aligned}w-0 & =(x-0)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(0,0,3)+(y-0)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(0,0,3)+(z-3)\frac{∂f}{∂z}(0,0,3) \\ w & =0x+0y+0(z-3) \\ w & =0\end{aligned}
$$
